package_info.package_versions: unknown (all known versions at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package 'redapty' is malicious because it contains code that, upon import, exfiltrates all environment variables from the victim's machine to an attacker-controlled server using an obfuscated (reversed) URL. The package is distributed as a dependency of a typosquatted package ('pampyio'), which uses the StarJacking technique to appear legitimate by linking to a popular but unrelated GitHub repository. This combination of supply chain deception and stealthy data exfiltration poses a significant threat to users.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reverses a hardcoded string to reconstruct an attacker-controlled HTTPS URL, concatenates all current environment variables as a string, and sends an HTTP GET request to the remote server, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive environment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it programmatically accesses all environment variables and transmits them to an external server without user knowledge or consent. The use of string reversal to obfuscate the destination URL is a deliberate evasion technique to bypass static analysis and detection tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package code should not access or transmit environment variables to external servers, especially not automatically at import-time and without explicit user consent. Additionally, normal packages do not obfuscate network destinations or perform hidden data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may collect limited, non-sensitive environment data for telemetry or debugging, but this is always opt-in, clearly documented, and never obfuscated. Full environment variable exfiltration is never justified in normal package behavior.
key_indicators: Obfuscated (reversed) hardcoded URL string in code
Access and serialization of all environment variables
Network request to an attacker-controlled domain at import-time
No user interaction or consent required for exfiltration
Execution of network exfiltration logic in __init__.py

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a typosquatted package ('pampyio') that mimics the popular legitimate package ('pampy'), using the StarJacking technique to link to the real project's GitHub repository and appear trustworthy.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased likelihood of developer installation due to perceived popularity and legitimacy.

attack_chain.action: The typosquatted package ('pampyio') declares a dependency on the malicious package ('redapty').
attack_chain.leads_to: Automatic installation of the malicious dependency when 'pampyio' is installed.

attack_chain.action: Upon import of the malicious dependency ('redapty'), the code in 'aptyred/__init__.py' executes, exfiltrating environment variables to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive environment data from victim systems.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time network requests to external domains from package code
Presence of obfuscated or reversed URL strings in Python source files
Access to and exfiltration of all environment variables
Dependencies with no legitimate functionality but containing network exfiltration logic
file_indicators: aptyred/__init__.py containing obfuscated network exfiltration code
setup.py or setup.cfg referencing unrelated or popular GitHub repositories (StarJacking)
Packages with names similar to popular packages (typosquatting), e.g., 'pampyio' vs 'pampy'
network_indicators: HTTP(S) requests to 'whiteevil1990.herokuapp.com' (or its obfuscated/reversed forms)
Unusual GET requests containing serialized environment variable data in the URL
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that make network requests at import-time or installation-time, especially those sending environment variables or using obfuscated URLs. Flag packages whose setup.py/setup.cfg references a GitHub repository unrelated to the package's codebase. Detect typosquatted package names and dependencies that lack legitimate functionality but contain network exfiltration logic. Use static analysis to identify reversed or obfuscated URL strings and code accessing os.environ in __init__.py files.
